what: Review of a DRAFT amendment to PREREGISTRATION.md, 2026-11-21. The draft would have changed how criterion C3 is carried out: every module replayed by rhv-replay, and leanchecker run on a fixed sample of 2,000 modules and on the 114 prefix modules. Four AI reviewers read the draft and the code that went with it, one lens each (wording precision, facts, code against text, hostile referee); for two of the lenses a second agent re-checked the findings. Their text is given as returned, apart from the removal of private paths. 51 findings in all.
outcome: The amendment was NOT made. PREREGISTRATION.md is unchanged and still ends with 'No amendments'. Two things in the review decided that. First, findings that the scripts of the time let a rejection be erased by a later passing run or by compiling the module again, and tied results to no particular program: an amended criterion resting on those scripts would have been weaker than its text claimed. Second, the hostile referee's point that the cost which motivated the amendment came from what was on leanchecker's search path, not from leanchecker: with only a module's import closure on the search path the stock tool can cover every module in about the time the second program takes (docs/performance-notes.md, section 10). The scripts were then changed to do that and to keep every result; the sample list and the options the draft refers to (replay-sample-list, scripts/verify/c3_stock_sample.txt, the two-part --c3) were withdrawn and are not in the repository.
status_of_the_draft: A text that was considered and set aside. It is kept here so that the findings can be read against what they are about. It has no force and nothing in the repository depends on it.
draft_as_reviewed_NOT_ADOPTED:
### Amendment 1, 2026-11-21 (UTC): how criterion C3 is carried out

Everything above this heading is the document as registered, byte for byte, including the line "No amendments", which was true then. The registered text is commit `39c6e1d` of this repository, release `prereg-v1`, DOI `10.5281/zenodo.24410554`. This amendment was added before any replay of the whole tree had been run by any tool.

**What changes.** Only how C3 is carried out. C1, C2, the rules of section 4 and the outcomes of section 5 stand as written.

**Why.** C3 says that every compiled module is re-checked by `leanchecker`. After registration it was measured that `leanchecker`, before it checks anything, lists every compiled file on its search path, once per process; run once per module, that listing is repeated for every module and grows with the tree. With 32 checks at a time on a rented 32-thread machine a check took 4.4 seconds with 1,792 modules compiled and 8.5 seconds with 29,633. Carried to 175,187 modules that is 43 to 56 hours for the replay alone on that machine, and weeks on the 24 GB machine the first build runs on. The same replay without the listing took 3.1 seconds per module in a rehearsal, about 6 hours for the tree. The measurements, the estimate and its limits are in `docs/performance-notes.md`, section 10, and `records/cloud/replay_cost.json`. The reason for the change is this cost. It is not a result of any replay: none had failed.

**C3 as amended.** An independent kernel replay agrees, established as follows.

(a) *Every compiled module of the project is replayed by `rhv-replay`.* That is the program built with the pinned toolchain from `scripts/verify/replay/RhvReplay.lean` of this repository, a file whose SHA-256 is `52c1984827f2c461ce4c7db782076a1d47cce8875657722556ae62d26a7bc3ef`. It contains the function `replayFromImports`, which is what `leanchecker` runs on each module it checks, copied from `src/lean/LeanChecker.lean` of the pinned toolchain; before every run the copy is compared, character for character, with that file in the toolchain as installed (1,131 characters, SHA-256 `4a1a5a15aa9296ca7fa05bc6fae5413962b27b718ab9acf1b50b6c461bbe7464`). The program differs from `leanchecker` in how the modules to check are chosen: it is given exact module names and finds each compiled file directly.

(b) *`leanchecker` from the pinned toolchain re-checks two sets of modules.* First, the 2,000 modules listed in `scripts/verify/c3_stock_sample.txt`, a file whose SHA-256 is `73647327c7ab3aa2e2aa5d8718dad9025d15b86d027a9f17fba235b7340f773d`, each in a process of its own. The list was fixed when this amendment was written: the 175,073 modules of the source tree whose name is not a prefix of another module's name, sorted, from which Python's `random.Random(20261120).sample` drew 2,000 (`scripts/verify/rhv_tools.py replay-sample-list` makes the list again from the source tree; the file is the definition). Second, each of the 114 modules whose name is a prefix of another module's name, in one process together with every module beneath it, which is how `leanchecker` treats such a name; the check of such a module passes only if `leanchecker` exits with status 0 and reports having replayed that module.

(c) *C3 holds if and only if* every compiled module has passed (a); every module of the list and every prefix module has passed (b); and no module has been failed by either tool. A module passed by one tool and failed by the other fails C3, and the disagreement is reported. A result counts only for the compiled file it was obtained on: if a module is compiled again, its earlier results are void.

The rule of section 4 for telling a failure of the proof from a failure of the machine applies to both tools as it does to the compiler: a checker that was killed from outside, or that could not open or find a compiled file, has not tested the module and is run again; a module is recorded as failing only when a tool rejects it, or crashes on it, reproducibly. Both tools are run with `LEAN_ABORT_ON_PANIC=1`, so that an internal error of the Lean runtime ends the process and is recorded, in place of printing a message and carrying on. If the replay cannot be completed with the resources available, C3 is neither met nor failed and the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE, as for a build that cannot be completed.

`scripts/09_kernel_replay.sh --c3` runs (a) and (b) and reports each condition of (c).

**What this gives up.** Under C3 as registered, the program that examines every module is the binary shipped with the toolchain. Under C3 as amended, that binary examines 2,000 modules chosen at random in advance and the 114 prefix modules with the modules beneath them; every other module is examined by a program built locally from about fifty lines of this repository and the toolchain's libraries. The function that does the examining is the same source text in both, and section 6 already lists the toolchain as trusted; what is added to that list is the correctness of those fifty lines outside the copied function, which is a loop that calls it and prints the result, and of the scripts that record what it prints. Nothing is made stronger by this amendment.

C3 as registered can still be carried out by anyone with the time: `scripts/09_kernel_replay.sh` with no option runs `leanchecker` on every module. Results are recorded by tool, and the summary reports separately whether `leanchecker` alone has passed every module. If that is ever done, it will be reported beside the amended criterion.

**What was known when this was written** (2026-11-21, about 15:00 UTC).

- No module had failed to compile on any machine. On the first machine 57,205 of 175,187 modules had compiled. On rented machines, a pilot had compiled 29,633 modules, including modules importing up to 17,860 others, and four rehearsals had each compiled between 1,642 and 1,796.
- The headline theorem had not been compiled anywhere. Whether C1 or C2 holds was not known.
- No replay of the whole tree had been run by either tool, and no module had failed a replay by either tool.
- `leanchecker` had passed every module it had been run on: samples of 24 and 30 on the first machine; 565 in the pilot's rehearsal and 2,233 in the pilot; all 1,792 compiled files of one rehearsal of the full run; and 150 in another.
- `rhv-replay` had passed every module it had been run on: 140 on the first machine and the 1,794 finished modules of one rehearsal. On 180 modules both tools had been run on the same compiled file, with the same verdict each time.
- All of those modules are from the lower part of the import graph. `rhv-replay` had not been run on a module with a large import closure on the rented machine.
- The program and the scripts around it had been reviewed twice by AI agents (`records/cloud/replay_method_review.json`, `records/cloud/replay_method_recheck.json`) and tested with injected faults on a small project. They had not been reviewed by a person.

findings.title: A rejection is erased by any later pass: the summary keeps only the last result, and every run re-runs failed modules automatically
findings.where: Draft: 'a module is recorded as failing only when a tool rejects it, or crashes on it, reproducibly' and (c) 'no module has been failed by either tool'. Code: scripts/verify/rhv_tools.py replay_state, line 812 `latest[(f[0], method)] = f`; scripts/09_kernel_replay.sh lines 193 and 220 always plan with --retry-failed; full_guest.sh loops passes while modules remain.
findings.problem: The draft never says what 'reproducibly' means, how many re-runs there are, or who decides. The code decides it for you: only the last result per (module, tool) counts, and every invocation of 09_kernel_replay.sh (and so every pass of --c3 and of the cloud loop) re-runs modules whose last result was a failure. A module that one tool rejects, or that the two tools disagree on, becomes 'passed' as soon as one later attempt passes, and the summary then shows FAILED 0 and 'no module failed by either tool: yes'.
findings.evidence: In a scratch tree (<SCRATCH>/r4lens.3WnU), results.tsv held C rejected (status 1) by rhv-replay and by leanchecker, then passed by both on the same stamp. replay-summary --check-list --require-c3 printed 'FAILED: 0', 'no module failed by either tool: yes', and every condition yes apart from the list hash (a test artifact). With the published list all_hold would be true.
findings.why_it_matters: The kernel is deterministic on a given file. A rejection that does not come back means a fault in the machine or in the tooling, and it should never turn quietly into a pass. As things stand, retrying until a pass is the default behaviour, so VERIFIED can be reported for a module the kernel rejected.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Replace the sentence in the draft with: "A module that a tool rejects, or crashes on (it ends by a signal other than those named below), is run by that tool twice more on the same compiled file. If either re-run rejects or crashes, the module has failed. If both pass, the rejection was not reproduced: it is reported with its full error in every outcome, and C3 is not met on that run until both tools have passed the module on another machine. No result is set aside by any other means, and nobody decides otherwise case by case." Code: in replay_state, keep every result line per (module, tool, stamp) instead of only the last. Treat a module as failed if any rejection on the current stamp was reproduced, or if it has fewer than two re-runs after a rejection. Add 'rejections_not_reproduced' as a condition that blocks all_hold. In replay-plan, re-run a rejected module only up to the two re-runs, never indefinitely.

findings.title: Compiling a module again voids its earlier rejections as well as its passes
findings.where: Draft (c): 'A result counts only for the compiled file it was obtained on: if a module is compiled again, its earlier results are void.' Code: rhv_tools.py status(), line 829 `if r[3] != stamps[mod]: return "stale"`, which is checked before the exit status.
findings.problem: Both the text and the code throw away a rejection once the module is compiled again. The code even keeps a failure when the .hash file is missing (line 826) but drops it when the stamp has changed, so the two cases are handled inconsistently. Recompiling is therefore a second way to clear a rejection.
findings.why_it_matters: If a rejected module is recompiled (by a later lake build, a repair, or an interrupted build resumed) and then passes, VERIFIED can be reported without the rejection ever appearing. This is the 'module recompiled between passes' loophole.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Replace with: "A pass counts only for the compiled file it was obtained on: if a module is compiled again, its earlier passes no longer count. An earlier rejection still counts. The module has failed C3, and the report gives the rejection and why the module was compiled again." Code: in status(), check for rc not in (0, NOT_RUN_STATUSES) on any earlier stamp before returning 'stale', and report such modules in a list that blocks all_hold.

findings.title: The C3 decision does not check which replay program produced the results
findings.where: Draft (a): rhv-replay 'is the program built with the pinned toolchain from scripts/verify/replay/RhvReplay.lean ... SHA-256 52c1…'. Code: 09_kernel_replay.sh accepts any binary through RH_REPLAY_DRIVER (only logged as a NOTE). replay-summary records rhv_replay_programs_used, but the c3_as_amended_2026_11_21 conditions (rhv_tools.py lines 333-340) do not include it. full_guest.sh reports every_recorded_run_used_this_program only as a separate fact.
findings.problem: The source check (replay-driver-check) ties the source file to the toolchain. It does not tie the binary that produced the results to that source. `--c3` can exit 0 and all_hold can be true for rhv-replay results produced by any program that prints REPLAY_OK. The list file is protected by a hash condition; the program has no equivalent.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the 'program replaced by another before the run' loophole. The amendment defines (a) by a specific program, but the code that decides whether (a) holds never checks that this program was the one used.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Add to (a): "Results of any other program do not count. Every run of rhv-replay records the SHA-256 of the program it used, and C3 holds only if every recorded run used one program, built in that run's setup from the file above after the comparison with the toolchain's source succeeded." Code: add to cond `"every_rhv_replay_run_used_the_checked_program": bool(programs) and len({p['sha256'] for p in programs}) == 1 and all(p['origin'] in ('built_here_from_the_checked_source', <the cloud's root-build origin>) for p in programs)`. In the cloud run, also require driver_check.txt to be present and to have succeeded before all_hold can be true.

findings.title: The stock binary never re-checks the module that holds the claimed theorem
findings.where: (b) and 'What this gives up'
findings.problem: `Main` (which holds riemannHypothesis) and `Statements` are not in c3_stock_sample.txt, and neither is a prefix module. Under the amendment, the toolchain's own leanchecker binary therefore never examines the module whose declaration is the claim under test. The 'What this gives up' paragraph does not say so.
findings.evidence: From records/source/import_graph.json.gz: 175,187 modules, 114 prefix modules, 175,073 eligible. random.Random(20261120).sample(sorted eligible, 2000), sorted, reproduces the committed list exactly. `grep -x 'Main\|Statements'` on the list finds nothing, and neither name is a prefix module. Main imports Statements and Supplements.Kernels.MainTheoremsAll, and its closure is the whole tree.
findings.why_it_matters: A careful reader will object that the one module that matters most is examined only by the locally built program. Fixing this now costs one or two leanchecker processes and does not depend on any result. C2 already imports Main into one environment on the same machine, so the memory needed is already being provided.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Add to (b), before 'Second': "Also, the modules `Main` and `Statements`, each in a process of its own." Code: append those two names to the stock pass (a second fixed list, or named in the --c3 and full_guest stock passes), and add a condition `named_modules_passed_by_leanchecker`. If the pinned list file must stay as it is, keep it unchanged and pin the two names separately.

findings.title: New INCONCLUSIVE trigger contradicts 'the outcomes of section 5 stand as written', and 'the replay' is ambiguous for part (b)
findings.where: 'What changes. ... the outcomes of section 5 stand as written' versus 'If the replay cannot be completed with the resources available, C3 is neither met nor failed and the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE'
findings.problem: Section 5 gives INCONCLUSIVE only for 'the build cannot be completed'. The draft adds a new case while saying section 5 is unchanged. 'The replay' could mean (a) only, or (a) and (b). In the cloud run, the leanchecker passes are simply skipped when under 120 s remain, a case the draft does not address. 'The resources available' is also undefined. And under the 'reproducibly' rule, a rejection seen just before the run ends would neither be a failure nor be reported.
findings.why_it_matters: Two honest readers could disagree about the outcome when (a) is complete but (b) is not. A rejection could also go unreported under INCONCLUSIVE.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Change 'What changes' to: "Only how C3 is carried out, and one addition to section 5: the outcome INCONCLUSIVE also covers a kernel replay that cannot be completed. C1, C2 and the rules of section 4 stand as written." Replace the INCONCLUSIVE sentence with: "If any part of (a) or (b) is not completed in a run, for whatever reason, C3 is not met in that run and, unless a module has failed, the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE. The report says which conditions of (c) were not established. Every rejection observed by either tool is reported in every outcome, whether or not it has been reproduced."

findings.title: 'Compiled module' and the set of files the results must come from are undefined, including whether results from other machines (such as the Mac build) count
findings.where: (a) 'Every compiled module of the project'; (c) 'the compiled file it was obtained on'
findings.problem: The draft never says that all 175,187 modules must be compiled. The code requires it (condition every_source_module_compiled_and_nothing_else, which also rejects compiled files without source and stray .olean.server/.olean.private parts), but the text does not. It also does not say whether results from different builds may be combined. Today the identity of a file is Lake's 64-bit content hash in <module>.olean.hash, which Lake writes when it writes the file. Nothing recomputes it at check time. Identical bytes from another machine would carry the same stamp, so a results.tsv copied from the Mac build would be credited to the cloud build's files.
findings.why_it_matters: This bears directly on the question of using the Mac work to reduce the cloud work. As drafted, a reader cannot tell whether Mac rhv-replay or leanchecker results may count towards the cloud build's C3. Whichever answer is intended must be fixed now, before results exist.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Add to (c): "Here a compiled module is one of the 175,187 modules of section 1, compiled in the build that establishes C1. C3 requires each of them to have a compiled file, and no compiled file without a source to exist. A compiled file is identified by the hash Lake writes beside it, and in the cloud run also by the SHA-256 of the file at the end of the run." Then choose one of the following and state it. Either "Only results obtained on the files of that build count", or "A result obtained on another build counts only if the file had the same SHA-256 as the file of the build that establishes C1, and each such result is listed with the machine it came from." Code: if the second is chosen, record the SHA-256 of each checked file in results.tsv, not only Lake's hash.

findings.title: The account of how rhv-replay differs from leanchecker, and of what is given up, is incomplete
findings.where: (a) 'The program differs from leanchecker in how the modules to check are chosen'; 'What this gives up'
findings.problem: rhv-replay also differs in how it runs. It replays up to 25 modules one after another in one process (kernel_check_batch.sh, --batch 25), waits for each replay before starting the next (its own header says so), and runs with LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1. leanchecker as used in (b) runs one module per process. So per-module process isolation is also given up, and state left by one replay could in principle affect the next. 'What this gives up' also leaves out two things. First, the decision that C3 holds is now made by replay-summary in rhv_tools.py, not by a tool's exit status. Second, the sample has limited power: with 2,000 of 175,073 modules, a disagreement between the tools on 0.15% of modules (about 260) escapes the sample with probability about 5%, and one confined to a few modules almost surely escapes.
findings.why_it_matters: 'What this gives up' is the paragraph a reader relies on to judge the trade, so it has to be complete. Leaving out the process model and the detection power makes the change look smaller than it is.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: In (a), replace the last sentence with: "The program differs from leanchecker in how the modules are chosen (it is given exact module names and finds each compiled file directly), and in that it replays several modules one after another in one process, one at a time." Add to 'What this gives up': "It also gives up running every module in a process of its own, and makes the program that reads the recorded results (`scripts/verify/rhv_tools.py replay-summary`) the judge of whether C3 holds. The 2,000 modules are a check that the two programs agree, not a second full replay. If they disagreed on fewer than about one module in 700, the list would probably not show it."

findings.title: It is unclear how C3 as amended relates to a full leanchecker run, or to results that arrive after a verdict
findings.where: 'C3 as registered can still be carried out ... If that is ever done, it will be reported beside the amended criterion.'
findings.problem: The draft does not say which criterion governs the verdict when the two disagree. A full leanchecker run might pass every module while rhv-replay rejected one, or C3 as amended might hold and a later leanchecker or rhv-replay run might reject a module of the same build. 'Reported beside' could be read as letting the more favourable result stand.
findings.why_it_matters: Two honest readers could reach different verdicts from the same results.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Replace with: "The verdict follows C3 as amended. A full leanchecker run does not replace it. A rejection by either tool of any module of the build that establishes C1, whenever it is obtained, including after a verdict, means C3 fails, and a VERIFIED verdict already given is withdrawn and the withdrawal reported."

findings.title: Nothing prevents a second amendment to C3 after replay results are known
findings.where: Whole amendment (section 8 allows further amendments that state what was known)
findings.problem: Section 8 lets amendments be made at any time as long as they say whether results were known. Nothing stops a later amendment from changing the list, the program or the pass/fail rules once rejections or INCONCLUSIVE results have been seen.
findings.why_it_matters: This loophole is the one a pre-registration exists to close: choosing the criterion after seeing the results.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Add: "After any replay of the whole tree has begun, how C3 is carried out will not be amended again in any way that could change whether a module counts as passed or failed. If any other change is made, the verdict will also be reported under this amendment as it stands, and the two will be given together."

findings.title: 'Nothing is made stronger' is not accurate
findings.where: 'What this gives up' last sentence
findings.problem: In some respects the amendment asks for more than C3 as registered. A rejection by rhv-replay fails C3 even if leanchecker passes the module. A crash counts as a failure, whereas section 4 for the compiler counts only Lean errors. Both tools run with LEAN_ABORT_ON_PANIC=1. The sentence presumably means that nothing offsets what is given up, but as written it is false.
findings.why_it_matters: A false sentence in a document that cannot be edited will draw an objection.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Replace with: "The amendment asks for more in two respects only: a rejection by rhv-replay also fails C3, and a crash of either tool counts as a failure. Neither makes up for what is given up."

findings.title: 'Killed from outside' and 'could not open or find' are not defined
findings.where: 'a checker that was killed from outside, or that could not open or find a compiled file, has not tested the module and is run again'
findings.problem: These phrases are defined only in the scripts: exit statuses 129, 130, 137 and 143, and status 96 for errors that begin with "failed to open file '", "object file '" or "unknown module prefix '". The text does not say that a module which keeps being killed is never passed.
findings.why_it_matters: Without the definition, 'killed from outside' reads as a catch-all for setting results aside.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Add: "'Killed from outside' means ended by the signals HUP, INT, KILL or TERM. 'Could not open or find a compiled file' means the tool's error begins with one of the three texts its own file handling writes, recorded as status 96. Any other non-zero ending is a rejection or a crash. A module whose checks keep ending these ways has not passed."

findings.title: The 1,131-character figure and its SHA-256 do not say exactly what text was hashed
findings.where: (a) '(1,131 characters, SHA-256 4a1a5a15…)'
findings.problem: The figure is for the text from `unsafe def replayFromImports` to the next definition, with trailing whitespace removed and one newline added (replay-driver-check). The function alone, without that final newline, is 1,130 characters with SHA-256 d5fd4cd4…, so a reader computing the obvious span cannot reproduce the published hash.
findings.evidence: replay-driver-check against ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.33.1/src/lean/LeanChecker.lean printed '1131 characters, sha256 4a1a5a15…'. Slicing the function from RhvReplay.lean gives 1,130 characters and d5fd4cd4….
findings.why_it_matters: A hash in an immutable document should be checkable without reading the code.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Write: "(the text from `unsafe def replayFromImports` up to the next definition, trailing blank lines removed and one newline added: 1,131 characters, SHA-256 4a1a5a15…)".

findings.title: 'What was known' does not give the seed's provenance or how much of the list had already been checked
findings.where: (b) list construction; 'What was known'
findings.problem: The seed 20261120 entered the repository in commit 6488d27 (2026-11-20 22:34 UTC), after registration, as the default of 09_kernel_replay.sh. The procedure of drawing from the source tree without prefix modules is new in this amendment. A reader cannot tell whether other seeds or procedures were tried, or whether any of the 2,000 listed modules had results already. The text also does not say that the prefix pass has never been run on a real prefix module on a rented machine (records/cloud/full-rehearsals/README.md, line 126).
findings.why_it_matters: This is what a reader needs to judge whether the list could have been chosen with results in view.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Add to 'What was known': "The seed is the default sample seed committed in 6488d27 on 2026-11-20. No other seed or way of drawing was tried. N of the 2,000 listed modules had been checked by either tool, all passing. The stock tool's prefix pass had been run on a seven-module project and by hand on two real prefix modules, but not on a rented machine." Fill in N from the records.

findings.title: The time kept for leanchecker on the 2,000 listed modules is about the projected need, with no margin
findings.where: cloud/gcp/full_guest.sh STOCK_ALLOW=2000 ('about a second a module on the whole tree')
findings.problem: replay_cost.json projects 30.1 s per leanchecker check on the whole tree at 32 at a time, which is about 1,880 s for 2,000 checks before any listed module with a large import closure. If the stock pass is squeezed or skipped (under 120 s left), C3 is INCONCLUSIVE and, with the default full-keep-oleans=0, the compiled files are gone.
findings.why_it_matters: The default cloud run could end without part (b) of C3 being established.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Reserve at least 1.5 x 2,000 x 30.1 / 32, about 2,800 s, or measure it in the trial windows. Set full-keep-oleans=1 for the full run, so that (b) can be finished later on the same files.

findings.title: "No module has been failed by either tool" is not what the code checks: a later pass erases an earlier failure
findings.where: Draft (c), "no module has been failed by either tool", and the section 4 sentence "a module is recorded as failing only when a tool rejects it, or crashes on it, reproducibly"; code: rhv_tools.py replay_state (latest[(f[0], method)] = f) and 09_kernel_replay.sh (plan_args="--retry-failed ..." on every run)
findings.problem: The draft's wording means a module fails if a tool has ever failed it. The summary keeps only the latest result for each (module, method). 09_kernel_replay.sh always plans with --retry-failed, so every later run, including a second --c3 and the cloud driver's repeat passes, replays modules that failed. If such a retry passes, the failure is gone from the summary and from c3_as_amended_2026_11_21; it survives only as an old line in results.tsv. The draft's "reproducibly" has no counterpart in the code either: one failure counts at once, and one later pass cancels it.
findings.evidence: rhv_tools.py replay_state: `latest[(f[0], method)] = f` (the last line wins); status() reads only that line. 09_kernel_replay.sh: `plan_args="--retry-failed --method $METHOD"`, and the prefix pass uses `--retry-failed --prefix-modules`. cmd_replay_plan with retry_failed treats only "passed" as done.
findings.why_it_matters: The kernel is deterministic, so a module that is rejected once and accepted later points to a fault that has to be reported. As things stand, re-running until a module passes would make every condition read "yes" and the result VERIFIED, while the draft says a failed module fails C3.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Text for (c): "...and no module's most recent result by either tool, for the compiled file now on disk, is a rejection or a crash. Any rejection or crash by either tool that did not recur when the module was run again is reported with the run in which it occurred, and C3 is not met until it is explained." Code: in replay_state, also collect for each method the modules that have ever had a failing or crashing line with the current stamp. Add the condition "no_module_ever_failed_on_the_current_file_by_either_tool" to the amended block, so that a later pass cannot clear it silently.

findings.title: The C3 conditions do not check that rhv-replay results came from the program defined in (a)
findings.where: Draft (a), "That is the program built with the pinned toolchain from scripts/verify/replay/RhvReplay.lean ..."; code: rhv_tools.py cond dict; 09_kernel_replay.sh RH_REPLAY_DRIVER branch
findings.problem: 09_kernel_replay.sh takes any binary through RH_REPLAY_DRIVER (origin "supplied_through_RH_REPLAY_DRIVER"). It checks only the source file, never the binary. The six conditions in c3_as_amended_2026_11_21 never look at replay_program.tsv. A run with some other binary would therefore show "every compiled module passed by rhv-replay: yes" and "all of these hold: yes". Only the cloud driver's facts.json compares hashes (every_recorded_run_used_this_program), and that is not part of --c3 or of the amended block.
findings.evidence: cond = {every_compiled_module_passed_by_rhv_replay, every_source_module_compiled_and_nothing_else, every_listed_module_passed_by_leanchecker, every_prefix_module_passed_by_leanchecker, no_module_failed_by_either_tool, the_list_is_the_published_one}. No condition uses `programs`. The fifth rehearsal's summary prints a program "supplied through RH REPLAY DRIVER".
findings.why_it_matters: (c) says C3 holds if and only if modules passed "(a)", where (a) names a specific program, yet the tool that reports (c) cannot tell whether that program was used.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Add a seventh condition: every run in replay_program.tsv used one program, with one SHA-256, that was either built here from the checked source or recorded by the run's own build of the checked source. In the draft, after (a), add: "The SHA-256 of the program used in each run is recorded beside the results, and a result from any other program does not count."

findings.title: "If a module is compiled again, its earlier results are void" is not what the stamp does
findings.where: Draft (c), last sentence: "A result counts only for the compiled file it was obtained on: if a module is compiled again, its earlier results are void."
findings.problem: Results are tied to the hash that the build tool keeps in the .hash file beside the .olean. That hash is read from the file, not recomputed. A module compiled again into the same bytes keeps the same stamp, so its earlier results still count. The script's own header says so: "if a module's imports were compiled again and its own compiled file came out byte for byte the same, its result still counts". So the sentence is false as written, and the stamp is not shown to identify the file unless something checks the .olean against its .hash.
findings.evidence: 09_kernel_replay.sh header lines 35-44; rhv_tools.py status(): `if r[3] != stamps[mod]: return "stale"`, where stamps are read from path + ".hash".
findings.why_it_matters: An immutable document should not promise behaviour the code does not have.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: "A result counts only for the compiled file it was obtained on, identified by the hash the build tool records beside that file. If that hash changes, earlier results for the module are void. A result counts only if it was obtained after the build had finished, with no compiled file rebuilt or replaced in between." (The cloud run's before-and-after hashing of every compiled file is what enforces the last clause.)

recheck_of_these_findings.title: "No module has been failed by either tool" is not what the code checks: a later pass erases an earlier failure
recheck_of_these_findings.reason: Confirmed in the code. rhv_tools.py replay_state keeps only the last line for each (module, method): `latest[(f[0], method)] = f`. status() and the amended block (`no_module_failed_by_either_tool: not failed`) read only that line. 09_kernel_replay.sh always plans with `--retry-failed` (lines 193 and 220), and cmd_replay_plan with retry_failed treats only "passed" as done. So a module that failed comes back on the next run, and a pass then removes the failure from the summary and from c3_as_amended_2026_11_21. This happens inside one unattended cloud run, not only across runs. full_guest.sh runs the trials, then `main`, then up to two `again` passes, and every one of them is a 09 run with --retry-failed. A kernel rejection in a trial or in the main pass that does not recur would leave no trace in the verdict. It would survive only as a raw line in results.tsv and in the phases_end count of non-zero lines, which also counts status 96. The draft's own section-4 sentence ('recorded as failing only when a tool rejects it ... reproducibly') can be read as allowing this. So both the text and the code need fixing: the kernel is deterministic, and a rejection that does not recur is itself a finding, not noise.
recheck_of_these_findings.fix: Draft (c): replace 'and no module has been failed by either tool' with 'and no tool has rejected or crashed on any module for the compiled file now on disk, in any run, whether or not the rejection recurred when the module was run again. Every such rejection or crash is reported with the run in which it occurred.' In the section-4 paragraph, change 'a module is recorded as failing only when a tool rejects it, or crashes on it, reproducibly' to 'a module is recorded as failing when a tool rejects it or crashes on it; a module is re-run only when the checker did not test it (killed from outside, or unable to open or find a compiled file).' Code: in replay_state, also collect for each method the set of modules that have any line with a failing or crashing status (not in NOT_RUN_STATUSES) whose stamp equals the current stamp. Add the condition `no_module_ever_rejected_or_crashed_on_the_current_file_by_either_tool` to the amended block, and print those modules under FAILED even when a later line passed.

recheck_of_these_findings.title: The C3 conditions do not check that rhv-replay results came from the program defined in (a)
recheck_of_these_findings.reason: 09_kernel_replay.sh accepts any executable through RH_REPLAY_DRIVER (origin `supplied_through_RH_REPLAY_DRIVER`). It checks only the source file with replay-driver-check, never the binary against that source. cmd_replay_summary reads replay_program.tsv into `programs` but only prints it. None of the six entries in `cond` uses it, so `all_hold` can be yes with a foreign binary. Result lines also carry no program identity, so a row cannot be tied to a program except through the timing of the runs. The cloud run always uses RH_REPLAY_DRIVER (root builds the program), so the amended block cannot tell its runs from an arbitrary binary. Only facts.json's every_recorded_run_used_this_program makes the comparison. Medium rather than high: getting this wrong takes a deliberate environment setting, and the origin is printed.
recheck_of_these_findings.fix: Code: add a seventh condition, `every_rhv_replay_run_used_the_program_built_from_the_checked_source`. It holds when replay_program.tsv exists, all its lines carry one SHA-256, and that hash equals the hash of a build from the checked source, recorded either by 09 (origin built_here...) or by the run's own setup build, which the cloud driver passes in, for example as RH_REPLAY_DRIVER_SHA256 checked at startup. Better still, write the program's SHA-256 as a seventh column of each rhv-replay result line, and count a line only if that hash is the accepted one. Draft, end of (a): 'The SHA-256 of the program used is recorded with every result, and a result obtained with any other program does not count.'

findings.title: A later pass wipes out an earlier rejection or crash. C3 then holds although a tool failed the module
findings.where: Draft (c): "no module has been failed by either tool", and the section-4 paragraph "a module is recorded as failing only when a tool rejects it, or crashes on it, reproducibly". Code: scripts/verify/rhv_tools.py replay_state (latest[(f[0], method)] = f, so the last line wins), cmd_replay_summary's "no_module_failed_by_either_tool": not failed; scripts/09_kernel_replay.sh plan_args="--retry-failed --method $METHOD", which every pass uses.
findings.problem: The summary keeps only the newest line for each (module, tool). Every run of 09, so every pass of --c3 and every 'again' pass in full_guest.sh, sends failed modules round again (--retry-failed is always set). If a module is rejected (status 1) or crashes (134, 139 and so on) and later passes on the same compiled file, the failure disappears. FAILED reads 0, no disagreement is reported, every condition reads yes and --require-c3 exits 0. Nothing in the code decides whether a failure is 'reproducible'. A failure just stops counting once a pass comes after it. The draft reads the other way: 'no module has been failed by either tool' means no failure was ever recorded.
findings.evidence: I built a synthetic tree of the 2,000 listed modules plus Zp and Zp.Q (so the list hash matches), with results files where (i) rhv-replay status 1 for a module precedes its pass, (ii) rhv-replay status 134 precedes a pass, (iii) leanchecker status 1 for a listed module precedes its pass. All three gave 'all of these hold: yes', 'FAILED: 0' and exit status 0 with --require-c3. Files are in <SCRATCH>/c3full.QX8w (flaky_rhv, crash_rhv, flaky_lc).
findings.why_it_matters: A tool that rejects a module once and accepts it on the next pass is exactly what C3 exists to catch. As written, the code turns it into VERIFIED with no trace in the summary, while the amendment says no failure occurred.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Code: in replay_state, keep for each (module, method, stamp) whether any line has a failing or crashing status (a status other than 0 and not in NOT_RUN_STATUSES), not just the newest line. A module with such a line for its current stamp goes in `failed` whatever came after. Add `modules_failed_then_passed` to the summary and JSON. Keep --retry-failed only so the re-run produces evidence, not so it overwrites. Text, replacing the last sentence of the section-4 paragraph: "Every result is kept. A module that either tool has rejected, or crashed on, in any run on its current compiled file has failed C3, even if a later run of the same tool passes it; the later result is reported beside the failure." If the owner wants a real reproducibility rule instead, the text must state it exactly (for example 'a failure is re-run twice; it counts unless both re-runs pass, and all three results are reported'), and the code must implement that rule, not latest-wins.

findings.title: all_hold does not check that the rhv-replay passes came from the pinned program
findings.where: Draft (a): "replayed by rhv-replay. That is the program built with the pinned toolchain from scripts/verify/replay/RhvReplay.lean ... SHA-256 52c19848...". Code: cmd_replay_summary's cond dict (no condition mentions `programs` or replay_program.tsv); 09_kernel_replay.sh accepts any binary through RH_REPLAY_DRIVER (it only logs a NOTE); kernel_check_batch.sh writes 'rhv-replay' in the method column with no program identity.
findings.problem: Every result line with method 'rhv-replay' counts towards condition (a), whatever program produced it. replay_program.tsv records one line per run (SHA-256 and origin), but the results are not tied to it line by line, and all_hold never reads it. A results file containing rhv-replay lines from an older RhvReplay.lean (an earlier rehearsal, before DRIVER_SHA256 changed), or from a binary named in RH_REPLAY_DRIVER, satisfies (a). full_guest.sh reports 'every_recorded_run_used_this_program' separately in facts.json, but `09 --c3` and the summary's 'all of these hold: yes' do not take it into account.
findings.evidence: In my synthetic test there was no replay_program.tsv at all, and the summary still printed 'every compiled module passed by rhv replay: yes' and 'all of these hold: yes', exit status 0.
findings.why_it_matters: Clause (a) is what allows the stock binary to be replaced for 173,000 modules. The only safeguard is that the program is the reviewed source. If the program's identity is not part of the check, condition (a) can be reported as met when it was not.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Code: add a seventh column to the rhv-replay result lines with the SHA-256 of the program that produced them (kernel_check_batch.sh already has RH_REPLAY_DRIVER). Count a line under (a) only if that SHA-256 belongs to a program recorded in replay_program.tsv as built from a source that passed replay-driver-check against DRIVER_SHA256. Record that fact too: the build step writes the binary's SHA-256 together with the checked source's SHA-256. Add the condition "every_rhv_replay_pass_is_by_the_pinned_program" to cond, so that all_hold depends on it. Text, add to (a): "A result of rhv-replay counts only if the results record that it was produced by a program built, by that run or by the cloud run's setup, from the file with the SHA-256 above, after the comparison."

findings.title: Damaged lines of the results file are dropped, and C3 can still hold
findings.where: rhv_tools.py replay_state: lines that are not complete are counted in `unreadable` and skipped; the cond dict has no condition on `unreadable`. The draft says nothing about damaged lines.
findings.problem: A line cut short (for example a failure line written while the disk was full) is ignored. The module then has no result, the next pass retries it, and a pass gives all_hold yes. The summary prints the count of ignored lines, but 'all of these hold' does not depend on it.
findings.evidence: Synthetic test 'damaged': two damaged status-1 lines for a module that had a passing line gave 'lines of the results file that are not a complete result (ignored): 2' and 'all of these hold: yes', exit status 0.

The modules concerned are run again, and any failure among those lines is treated as a recorded failure if it can be read." The first is the simpler and safer choice.

findings.title: Status 97 on a prefix module counts as a failure, which the amendment's own rule does not allow
findings.where: Draft (b): "the check of such a module passes only if leanchecker exits with status 0 and reports having replayed that module"; section-4 paragraph: "a module is recorded as failing only when a tool rejects it, or crashes on it, reproducibly". Code: kernel_check_one.sh sets rc=97 when the exit status is 0 but there is no 'replaying <mod>' line; 97 is not in NOT_RUN_STATUSES, so replay_state classifies it as 'failed'.
findings.problem: In this case leanchecker accepted everything it replayed but did not list the module. Nothing was rejected and nothing crashed. The draft says only that this is not a pass. The code records it as a failure of the module: 'no module failed by either tool: NO', FAILED lists the module, a disagreement with rhv-replay is reported, and the exit status is 1. Under section 5 that is NOT VERIFIED (C3 fails), reached through a case the amendment's rule says is not a failure.
findings.evidence: Synthetic test PREFIX97 in <SCRATCH>/c3lens.YCoI: conditions false were every_prefix_module_passed_by_leanchecker and no_module_failed_by_either_tool, rc=1. With 96 instead, only the prefix condition was false, rc=3.
findings.why_it_matters: The amendment would require NOT VERIFIED for something its own text classes as not a failure, or else leave the result to be argued after the fact.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Pick one and write it down. (1) Text: "If leanchecker exits with status 0 without reporting that it replayed the prefix module, the module has not been tested: it is run again, and while that stays so C3 is neither met nor failed." Code: treat 97 as not_run, or as a separate 'not_covered' state that blocks all_hold without counting as failed. (2) Alternatively, keep the code and add to the text: "...; if it exits with status 0 without reporting that module, this is recorded as a failure of the module."

findings.title: 'If a module is compiled again, its earlier results are void' is stronger than what the code can tell
findings.where: Draft (c): "A result counts only for the compiled file it was obtained on: if a module is compiled again, its earlier results are void." Draft: "scripts/09_kernel_replay.sh --c3 runs (a) and (b) and reports each condition of (c)." Code: the stamp is the content of Lake's '<module>.olean.hash', read when the run is planned and never recomputed; the 09 header says a byte-identical recompile keeps its results, and that an import compiled again does not void them.
findings.problem: (1) A module compiled again whose compiled file comes out byte for byte the same keeps its results, which contradicts 'void'. (2) A module whose imports were compiled again keeps results obtained against the old imports. (3) The hash is taken from Lake's file, not computed from the compiled file. A compiled file replaced while its .hash file stays the same keeps results obtained on the old content. full_guest.sh covers this by hashing every compiled file at the seal and at the end, but `09 --c3` does no such check, so the claim that it 'reports each condition of (c)' is not true for this clause.
findings.why_it_matters: The text promises a check the local tool does not carry out. A reader relying on '09 --c3 says every condition holds' would believe the results are tied to the files on disk when they are tied to Lake's record of them.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Text: "A result counts only for the content of the compiled file now on disk, as identified by the hash the build tool records beside it; a result recorded for other content does not count. The results that count must come from runs made after the build had finished, with no compiled file rebuilt or replaced between the first check and the last; the cloud run verifies this by hashing every compiled file before the checks and again after them." Then change the last sentence to: "scripts/09_kernel_replay.sh --c3 runs (a) and (b) and reports each condition of (c) except the last, which is established by the hashes taken before and after the checks." Alternatively, make --c3 hash every compiled file before pass 1 and after pass 3, and fail if anything changed.

findings.title: In facts.json, the main pass's exit status sits beside state DONE, and the verdict on amended C3 is buried in the summary
findings.where: cloud/gcp/full_guest.sh: C3_RC is the exit status of the rhv-replay main pass; facts 'c3_kernel_replay.last_exit_status' = C3_RC; c3_summary is called without --require-c3; the run ends with finish DONE "all phases ran". all_hold is found only at c3_kernel_replay.summary.c3_as_amended_2026_11_21.all_hold.
findings.problem: Suppose rhv-replay covers the tree, but the listed leanchecker pass is cut off by its time limit (status 124) or skipped ('under two minutes were left'). facts.json then shows state DONE, last_exit_status 0 (nothing failed, rhv-replay complete), and all_hold false three levels down. The say line 'kernel replay: last exit status 0' says the same. Nowhere at the top of the file does it say whether amended C3 holds.
findings.why_it_matters: The amendment makes the listed pass and the prefix pass part of the criterion. A run that did not finish them must not be easy to read as having met C3, and 'last_exit_status: 0' with 'DONE' invites exactly that reading.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: After the final c3_summary, run replay-summary once more with --check-list ... --require-c3, keep its status as C3_AMENDED_RC, and write top-level facts 'c3_as_amended_all_hold' (true or false) and 'c3_as_amended_exit_status' (0, 1 or 3). Rename 'last_exit_status' to 'main_pass_exit_status'. Change the final say line to report the amended status. When the listed pass or prefix pass was cut short or not run, make the finish message say "criterion C3 as amended not complete: <reason>" instead of only "all phases ran".

findings.title: The code adds a condition that clause (c) does not state: every source module compiled and nothing else
findings.where: Draft (c) lists: every compiled module passed (a); every listed and prefix module passed (b); no failure. Code: cond also has "every_source_module_compiled_and_nothing_else" (no source module uncompiled, no compiled module without source, no .olean.server/.olean.private files, no compiled file without a hash).
findings.problem: The code requires more than the text. Under the text alone, (a) holds vacuously for modules that were never compiled, and a partial build could formally satisfy C3. The code rightly refuses that, but the amendment is the definition and should say so.
findings.why_it_matters: The code should do what the amendment says, no more and no less. A reader comparing the two will find a condition the criterion does not contain.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Start (c) with: "C3 holds if and only if every module of the source tree is compiled, nothing else is compiled, and every compiled file has the hash the build tool writes beside it; every compiled module has passed (a); ..."

recheck_of_these_findings.title: A later pass wipes out an earlier rejection or crash. C3 then holds although a tool failed the module
recheck_of_these_findings.reason: The mechanism is real. replay_state keeps only the last line for each (module, method) (rhv_tools.py:812), and every plan uses --retry-failed (09_kernel_replay.sh:193, 220). But the reviewer reads the draft wrongly. Section 4 as registered says a module fails only if it fails 'reproducibly, on a re-run', and the amendment applies that rule to both tools. So one failure followed by a passing re-run (F,P) is not a failure under the text, and the code agrees with the text there. The real loophole is a failure that does reproduce. I tested this in <SCRATCH>/skep.uNRg/ffp.tsv: two rhv-replay status-1 lines for the same stamp, then a pass. The summary gave FAILED 0, all of these hold: yes, and exit 0 with --require-c3. A failure reproduced on re-run therefore still yields VERIFIED. Nothing in the text or the code says how many re-runs there are. Even an F,P case, which is an anomaly for a deterministic kernel, leaves no trace in the summary. The reviewer's fix ('any failure, ever, is permanent') goes against the registered 'reproducibly' rule and should not be adopted as written.
recheck_of_these_findings.fix: Text, replacing the last clause of the section-4 paragraph: 'a module that a tool rejects, or crashes on, is run again once by the same tool on the same compiled file; if that run also rejects it or crashes, the module has failed C3, whatever any later run shows. Every rejection and crash is reported, including one that a re-run did not repeat.' Code: in replay_state, count the failing or crashing lines (status not 0 and not in NOT_RUN_STATUSES) per (module, method, stamp), not just the last line. Two or more go in `failed` regardless of later passes. Exactly one, followed by a pass, goes in a new list `failed_once_then_passed`, printed in the summary and written to the JSON. The planner should re-run a module that has exactly one failure and stop re-running it once it has two.

recheck_of_these_findings.title: all_hold does not check that the rhv-replay passes came from the pinned program

And replay-driver-check checks the source in scripts/verify/replay, not the source that binary was built from. It is overstated as high for the verdict run, though. The cloud run starts with an empty results file, root builds one DRIVER in setup, and facts.json reports 'every_recorded_run_used_this_program' and 'unchanged_since_it_was_built'. The realistic gap is a results.tsv carried over between runs (for example on the Mac), where results from an earlier RhvReplay.lean still count because the stamps have not changed, and where `09 --c3` prints 'all of these hold: yes'. The draft's (a) defines rhv-replay as the program built from the file with SHA-256 52c19848... (that hash is correct), and the code does not enforce this.

Add cond 'every_rhv_replay_pass_is_by_a_program_built_from_the_pinned_source', true only if every rhv-replay line counted under (a) names a program that replay_program.tsv records as built from a source whose SHA-256 equals DRIVER_SHA256. findings.title: A rejection can be erased by a later pass or by recompiling the module; 'reproducibly' has no bound
findings.where: Draft (c): "no module has been failed by either tool" and "if a module is compiled again, its earlier results are void"; draft paragraph "a module is recorded as failing only when a tool rejects it, or crashes on it, reproducibly"; code: rhv_tools.py replay_state (`latest[(f[0], method)] = f`, and status() returning 'stale' before it looks at rc); 09 plan_args "--retry-failed"
findings.problem: The summary keeps only the last result per module and method. Every run of 09, including each --c3 pass and each loop of full_guest.sh, re-plans failed modules (--retry-failed). A rejection followed by one pass on the same compiled file therefore leaves nothing in FAILED and nothing in the report. A rejection on a file that is later compiled again becomes 'stale', also unreported. The draft makes this rule: earlier results, failures included, are void after a recompile, and 'reproducibly' is not bounded, so retrying until a pass is allowed.
findings.evidence: In my test tree I appended a leanchecker row with status 1 for Lib.B at its current stamp. The summary showed 'FAILED: Lib.B' and 'no module failed by either tool: NO'. I then appended a row with status 0 for the same stamp. The summary showed 'FAILED: 0' and 'no module failed by either tool: yes'. The kernel is deterministic (records/two-builds: two cloud builds identical to the byte), so a rejection that does not repeat is itself an anomaly a reader must be told about.
findings.why_it_matters: A referee will ask whether C3 could be passed by re-running until the tool said yes. As drafted, it could, and the record would not show it.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Draft, replace the last sentence of (c) with: "A pass counts only for the compiled file it was obtained on: if a module is compiled again, its earlier passes are void. A rejection or crash is never void. A module that either tool has rejected or crashed on is replayed once more by the same tool on the same compiled file. If that second run also rejects it, the module fails C3. If the second run passes it, the module still fails C3 unless the other tool also passes it on that file, and both results are reported with the module's name. Every rejection or crash recorded at any time, including on a file since compiled again, is listed in the report." Code: keep every row rather than only the last one, count any rejection or crash at any stamp in a new `ever_rejected` list, and add `no_unreported_rejection` (empty, or each entry meeting the rule above) to the conditions.

findings.title: The draft does not say why a way to keep leanchecker on every module was not taken
findings.where: Draft "Why." paragraph, from "leanchecker, before it checks anything, lists every compiled file on its search path" through "The reason for the change is this cost."
findings.problem: The cost comes from how leanchecker is invoked, not from the tool itself. Section 4 already lets 'where files are stored' vary. If each check is given a search path that holds only the project files in the module's import closure (mean 3,086) plus the libraries (10,452), the listing drops to about 13,500 files. That is close to the 12,244 of the third rehearsal, where a check took 4.4 s, so roughly 7 hours for the tree with the registered binary. Paying for a longer run, or using a second machine, were also open: the 42-hour limit is a setting chosen in cloud/gcp/pilot_local.sh (MAXRUN=151200), and the difference is about 73 USD (118 against 45 in replay_cost.json). performance-notes section 10 'What does not solve it' rules out only prefix batching and many modules per process.
findings.evidence: On a copy of prune-test, `LEAN_PATH=<dir holding copies of only Lib/A.olean and Lib/B.olean> leanchecker -v Lib.B` printed 'replaying Lib.B' and exited 0. Symlinked files or a symlinked directory gave 'Could not find any oleans' (findAllWithExt does not follow them), so hard links or copies would be needed. The timing at scale is my projection from the fit, not a measurement.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft's sole stated reason is cost. A referee who finds a cheap route that keeps the registered criterion will read the amendment as avoidable, which is the goalpost charge.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Add after "It is not a result of any replay: none had failed.": "Other ways of keeping `leanchecker` for every module were available and were not taken: a run of about 63 billed hours and 118 USD in place of about 24 hours and 45 USD, which needs a longer limit than the 42 hours this project set for a run; a second machine running `leanchecker` on the compiled files; or giving each `leanchecker` process a search path that holds only its module's imports, which is untested at scale and needs every file copied or hard-linked per check. They were not taken because [the owner's actual reason: for example, time to a result, or the untested link-farm machinery being itself new code in the path]. Any of them would carry out C3 as registered. The project does not claim that the amendment was the only way." The owner must fill in the bracket truthfully.

findings.title: What the 2,000-module sample can and cannot detect is not stated
findings.where: Draft (b) and "What this gives up" ("that binary examines 2,000 modules chosen at random in advance")
findings.problem: The draft never says what the sample is for or how strong it is. It checks the program, not the proof: a bad module that rhv-replay rejects already fails C3 through (a). The sample only catches the case where rhv-replay wrongly passes something leanchecker would reject, and only if that happens on enough modules. With 2,000 of 175,073 drawn without replacement, a defect that wrongly passes k modules is caught with probability 1.14 percent for k=1, 10.9 percent for k=10, 68 percent for k=100 and 95 percent for k=262 or more (0.15 percent of the tree). A defect confined to a few modules, to the deepest modules (the sample's maximum depth is 149 against 203 in the tree), or to modules with a particular content would almost never be caught.
findings.evidence: Computed exactly (hypergeometric) from N=175,073 and n=2,000. Depths were computed from records/source/import_graph.json.gz.
findings.why_it_matters: Without this, '2,000 of 175,073' reads either as a 1 percent re-check of the proof (wrong) or as arbitrary. A referee will compute these figures, and the amendment should state them first.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Add to "What this gives up": "The second tool's pass tests the program, not the proof: a module that rhv-replay rejects fails C3 whatever the sample shows. The sample can only show rhv-replay passing a module that `leanchecker` rejects. If no module of the list shows that, a fault that would make rhv-replay wrongly pass 262 or more modules (0.15 percent of the tree) is ruled out at 95 percent confidence. Any single module has a 1.1 percent chance of being on the list. So a fault in rhv-replay that affects only a few modules, or only modules with some rare property, would most likely not be found by the sample. Against such a fault, C3 as amended rests on reading the program, not on the second tool."

C1, C2 and every other rule and outcome stand as written."

findings.title: The stated reason gives hours but not the binding constraint, the price difference, or how thin the estimate is
findings.where: Draft "Why." paragraph: "Carried to 175,187 modules that is 43 to 56 hours ... The reason for the change is this cost."
findings.problem: Hours matter only against a limit, and the draft does not say what the limit is (a 42-hour run limit the project set) or what the difference costs (about 118 against 45 USD expected; 136 at the high end). It also does not say, in the amendment itself, that the stock tool's figure is a line through two measurements, that rhv-replay's 6 hours come from one rehearsal on the first hundredth of the tree, and that neither tool has been timed on deep modules. Nor does it say what happens if a full run shows the premise wrong.
findings.evidence: records/cloud/replay_cost.json whole_run.by_method; cloud/gcp/pilot_local.sh MAXRUN=151200 ('Google deletes the VM at 42 h'); CLAIMS.md: 'M8 and M9 rest on two measurements and a straight line.'
findings.why_it_matters: 'Cost' with no constraint or dollar figure looks like a pretext. Stating the actual numbers lets the reader judge whether the trade was reasonable.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Add after "about 6 hours for the tree.": "On the project's estimate (records/cloud/replay_cost.json), a full run would take about 63 billed hours and 118 USD with `leanchecker` on every module (60 to 73 hours, up to 136 USD), against about 24 hours and 45 USD under this amendment. This project limits a cloud run to 42 hours. The stock tool's figure is a line through two measurements made with at most 29,633 modules compiled, and rhv-replay's rests on one rehearsal on the first hundredth of the tree; neither tool has been timed on the whole tree. If a full run shows that `leanchecker` would have fitted after all, the report will say so; the amendment is not withdrawn on that ground."

findings.title: The draft does not say who wrote the criteria, the program and the amendment, or that the code implementing the amendment has not been reviewed
findings.where: Draft, last bullet of "What was known": "The program and the scripts around it had been reviewed twice by AI agents ... They had not been reviewed by a person."
findings.problem: (1) The criteria, this amendment, rhv-replay and the scripts that record and judge its results all come from the same project, and the reviews were by AI agents. The draft does not say the program was written by the same hands, or with AI help, which is what a referee means by independence. (2) The two review records cover the code of 2026-11-20. They do not cover the code added with this amendment: --c3, --check-list/--require-c3, the c3_as_amended conditions, replay-sample-list and the list. That code has the defects in the two high findings above.
findings.evidence: replay_method_review.json and replay_method_recheck.json are dated 2026-11-20 and describe the pre-amendment code. The --c3 changes are uncommitted (`git status`: M scripts/09_kernel_replay.sh, M scripts/verify/rhv_tools.py, ?? scripts/verify/c3_stock_sample.txt).
findings.why_it_matters: An amendment that loosens a criterion and is judged by code written alongside it, by the same party, is exactly what a hostile referee suspects. Saying so plainly is the answer.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Replace the bullet with: "The criteria, this amendment, rhv-replay and the scripts that run both tools and judge their results were all written by this project, [with the help of AI coding agents — the owner to confirm]. No one outside the project has reviewed any of them. The program and the scripts as they stood on 2026-11-20 had been reviewed twice by AI agents (records/cloud/replay_method_review.json, replay_method_recheck.json) and tested with injected faults on a small project. The code added with this amendment (`--c3` and the conditions the summary reports) had been reviewed by AI agents only [the record, once made], and by no person."

findings.title: How a VERIFIED reached under the amended C3 will be labelled, and what a later leanchecker failure does, is left open
findings.where: Draft paragraph "C3 as registered can still be carried out by anyone with the time ... If that is ever done, it will be reported beside the amended criterion."
findings.problem: (c) makes any failure by either tool fail C3. But the draft does not say that a failure found later, after a verdict, withdraws the verdict. It does not commit the report to saying that C3 was carried out as amended, or whether 'leanchecker alone on every module' holds. A reader could meet an unqualified VERIFIED.
findings.evidence: rhv_tools.py already computes complete_by_leanchecker_alone; the draft promises only to report it 'if that is ever done'.
findings.why_it_matters: The reader of a VERIFIED headline must be able to tell which C3 it rests on. A referee will also ask whether a later stock-tool failure is binding.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Add: "Every report of the verdict will say that C3 was carried out as amended by this amendment, and whether `leanchecker` alone has passed every module (C3 as registered). If `leanchecker` or rhv-replay later rejects any module of the tree that the verdict rested on, C3 fails and a verdict of VERIFIED is withdrawn and reported as such."

findings.title: The result is tied to the module's own compiled file, not to the files it imports; the amendment does not say so
findings.where: Draft (c): "A result counts only for the compiled file it was obtained on"
findings.problem: A limit documented in the header of 09_kernel_replay.sh and left open on purpose after review F-list says that a recorded result is tied to the module's own compiled file, not to its imports'. The amendment's condition reads as if the result were for the module as replayed.
findings.evidence: docs/performance-notes.md section 10: "one, which is stated as a limit in the header of scripts/09_kernel_replay.sh: a recorded result is tied to the module's own compiled file, not to its imports'."
findings.why_it_matters: This is part of what C3 as amended means. Under section 4's no-change rule and the end-of-run hash check it is not a practical gap, but it should be stated where the criterion is.
findings.proposed_text_or_fix: Append to (c): "A result is tied to the module's own compiled file; that the files it imports did not change after it was replayed is shown by the end-of-run check that every compiled file is as it was when the tree was sealed."
